messages:
maria-infra: Heads up — seeing a spike of GPU nodes in us-west2 marking NotReady / NoSchedule. cluster-autoscaler isn't replacing them. Anyone else? :warning:
infra-bot: [alert] node/usw2-gpu-pool-12 went NotReady (nvidia-device-plugin crashloop) at 2026-03-14T09:22:31Z
kai: Started looking. device-plugin logs show repeated registration timeouts.
kai: log excerpt:
```
E03014 09:21:57.123456 1 device_plugin.go:213] failed to register device plugin: timeout after 10s
I0314 09:21:57.123789 1 plugin_monitor.go:88] restarting device plugin container
```
sam: kubelet journal shows /dev/nvidia0 missing and kubelet marking allocatable gpu 0.
sam: `journalctl -u kubelet | grep -i nvidia` ->
```
Mar 14 09:20:40 node kubelet[1234]: failed to start device plugin: no devices found
Mar 14 09:20:45 node kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
```
alexa: That kernel mismatch message rings a bell — looks like the node image and the driver kernel module are out of sync after recent kernel patch.
alexa: Short-term: cordon affected nodes so schedulers stop placing new pods, then restart the nvidia-driver-installer DaemonSet with a bumped image that includes matching kernel headers.
alexa: Patch we applied in test cluster:
```
kubectl -n kube-system set env ds/nvidia-driver-installer DRIVER_TIMEOUT=120
kubectl rollout restart ds/nvidia-driver-installer
```
oncall: FYI cluster-autoscaler is refusing to scale because there are pods with nodeAffinity to GPU taints; it's waiting for nodes to be Ready. We might need to temporarily relax affinity or allow scale up to a different pool.
jordan: Also seeing cost impact — us-west2 GPU capacity is limited; autoscaler can't add more GPU machines due to regional quota. If we force scale up we risk running over budget.
maria-infra: Suggestion: 1) patch DS to increase timeout and restart, 2) cordon+drain failing nodes ignoring daemonsets, 3) open quota request for us-west2 GPUs with cloud provider, 4) set autoscaler to prefer fallback CPU pool for lower-priority jobs.
kai: Agreed. Also add a health check in driver-installer that writes `nvidia.com/gpu.present=true` label once devices are ready so autoscaler sees the assignment.
sam: I've created infra ticket INF-4238 and attached logs. If we can't fix quickly, we should promote CPU fallback for non-SLA traffic to reduce cost and customer impact.
maria-infra: I'll coordinate with oncall to run the restart commands in canary first. @oncall please confirm when you can take this.
oncall: On it, starting canary now, will post results in 10m.
maria-infra: thx :thumbsup:
